name: Supramolecular Chemistry
tagline: Self-assembly, host-guest chemistry, and non-covalent interaction design.
seo_title: Supramolecular Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Supramolecular Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in molecular recognition, self-assembly, host–guest chemistry and molecular machines.

definition.lead: Supramolecular chemistry is chemistry beyond the molecule: it studies how molecules recognize, bind and assemble through non-covalent interactions.
definition.body: Hydrogen bonds, π-stacking, metal coordination and the hydrophobic effect let molecules form host–guest complexes, self-assembled cages and even molecular machines. Nature uses the same tools to fold proteins and pair DNA strands.

quiz.q: Which of these are non-covalent interactions?
options: Hydrogen bonds, π-stacking and van der Waals forces
A larger host binds a smaller guest
A ring threaded onto an axle with bulky stoppers
Two rings linked together like a chain
A molecule that spins like a top
A long polymer chain with side groups

quiz.q: Feringa's molecular motor is driven by…

quiz.q: Why are reversible bonds useful in self-assembly?
options: Structures can correct mistakes as they form, and materials can self-heal
They are stronger than covalent bonds
